title: Command-Line Arguments
instructions: Programs can receive words typed after their name on the command line. main can take two parameters to catch them:
- argc is how many words there are (the program's own name counts as one).
- argv is the list of those words, as strings. argv[0] is the program name, argv[1] is the first real argument.
This practice window runs your program with no extra words, so you'll just see the program name. To see more, run it in a terminal like:  myprog hello world
Get it to compile and run here.
task: Fill in the loop body to print each argument with %s. (It just needs to run here.)
hint:
Print the i-th word:

        printf("word %d: %s\n", i, argv[i]);
